newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says not to blame for stalled Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says not to blame for stalled Hebron talks.

text.p: An Egyptian official said in remarks published on Friday that Egypt was not to blame for lack of progress in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and denied it was pressuring Palestinians to stall in the negotiations.
An official quoted in the government daily Al-Ahram was responding to remarks published on Thursday by Israel's ambassador to Washington, Eliahu Ben-Elissar.
"Israel's stance is the main reason behind the failure to achieving progress in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations," the official source said.

Al-Ahram said the official was commenting on Ben-Elissar's remarks in the Washington Times in which he accused Egypt of encouraging Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to stall an accord on the Israeli pullout from Hebron and of pressing other Arab countries not to normalise relations with Israel.
Negotiations on the withdrawal, which Israelis have delayed by 10 months, have stalled as Israelis and Arabs accuse each other of wrecking any hope for peace.
The Egyptian source said Ben-Elissar "has a vast imagination and he is far from the facts".

"Repeated statements by Israeli officials about the Egyptian 'obstructive' stance to reaching agreement on Hebron has become an old song and a cover for Israeli failure to take a step acceptable to the parties of the peace process," he said.

"Egypt did not accept in the past and will not accept in the future to impose on the Palestinians what they themselves reject. Whoever thinks Egypt could play a role contradictory to the authority of a just and balanced peace, and one which preserves the legitimate rights of the region's people, is disillusioned," the Egyptian official said.
